answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a meaningful stake in a shared vault before it can trade. Think of the vault as basalt bedrock under the market: one identity, one locked deposit, and misbehaviour slashes it. A single attacker can still afford one marble, but forging a thousand identities means funding a thousand deposits, so the cost of a fake crowd rises linearly while the gain from any one fake stays small, making sybil attacks unprofitable.
